campaign_id: qwen35-4b-w4a16 d1s/d2s: the strict-suite depth axis completed at depths 1 and 2 (2026-09-09)
question: The 2026-09-08 sweep ran the strict suite at depths 3, 4, 5 and 6 and found all four lossless with 3 and 4 tied at the top. Depths 1 and 2 were never run there, so the lane could say depth 3 is the best of 3-6 without knowing whether something shallower was as good.
config: one B70, TP1, draft INT4 head, pad off, FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture 1-64, strict 12-prompt six-class realistic suite over completions, 512-token cap, class-balanced median tok/s over tokens 1-100 after TTFT, two fresh servers per arm
finding_1_every_depth_is_lossless: All seven settings pass every gate: G1 on the MTP0 pair, G2 on the candidate pair, and G3 against the MTP0 oracle twice, 12/12 each. Speculation on this model and kernel is lossless on the strict suite at every depth from 1 to 6, which completes the axis rather than extending it.

finding_2_the_plateau_is_wider_than_publ.statement: The 2026-09-08 sweep described depths 3 and 4 as tied at the top. Depth 2 belongs in that group: 176.20 and 176.28 against depth 3's 177.41 and 177.17, a 0.7% difference. The plateau is depths 2 through 4, and only depth 1 at 1.47x is clearly below it.
finding_2_the_plateau_is_wider_than_publ.caveat: 0.7% is larger than the within-arm spread, which is 0.05% for depth 2 and 0.14% for depth 3, and smaller than this host's documented ~3% back-to-back drift. Depth 3 is very slightly ahead single-user; it is not a difference to choose on.

finding_3_depth_2_may_be_the_better_defa.statement: Single-user, depth 2 gives up 0.7% against depth 3. At c64 it returns 1364.4 tok/s against depth 3's 1200.3, which is 14% more, with an identical identity cost - the depth dose-response showed the oracle-free rate flat at 7.07% and 7.37% across depths 1, 2, 3 and 6.
finding_3_depth_2_may_be_the_better_defa.reading: For a server that sees any meaningful concurrency, depth 2 dominates depth 3: it is level single-user and materially better under load. The published operating point of depth 3 was chosen from a sweep that never measured depth 2.
finding_3_depth_2_may_be_the_better_defa.not_a_recommendation_to_change_the_packa: This is one comparison on one card. The packaged headline is a strict-suite single-user number where depth 3 is legitimately, if marginally, the fastest. Changing the operating point is a packaging decision that wants its own replication, and it was out of scope tonight.

closes_the_requested_axis: The campaign was asked for MTP 0, 1, 2 and 3. Depths 0 and 3 were already published; 1 and 2 are measured here to the same standard, on the same suite, with the same gates.
